Frequently Asked Questions

items.q: I’m curious but have never tried acupuncture before, will this be ok for me?

a.text: Yes, absolutely. This workshop is designed for those curious about and new to acupuncture and want to experience the healing benefits in a safe, supportive and professional environment.

items.q: How does acupuncture work?

a.text: Acupuncture works by stimulating the body’s natural healing processes, improving circulation and the flow of energy, reducing inflammation, and releasing endorphins (natural pain-relieving substances, reducing stress and improving your sense of well-being through the insertion of fine, sterile needles into specific points on the body.

items.q: Does acupuncture hurt?

a.text: The sensation of acupuncture needles can vary from person to person. Some people report feeling a slight pinch or discomfort when the needles are inserted, while others feel no pain at all. Most people find acupuncture to be a very relaxing and pain-free experience.

items.q: Are needles sterilized?

a.text: All needles are single-use, sterilized, and disposed of after each treatment.

items.q: Who should not join this workshop?

a.text: Pregnant women in their 1st trimester, anyone with uncontrolled high blood pressure, epilepsy, or severe heart conditions and anyone with open wounds, active infections, or fever on the day of the workshop should not join.

items.q: How should I prepare for this workshop?

a.text: Before the session, please:
– Avoid alcohol or recreational drugs for at least 24 hours
– Try not to eat heavy meals 1–2 hours before treatment (a light snack is fine)
– Wear comfortable, loose clothing so the therapist can easily access acupuncture points
– ⁠⁠No coffee 4 hours before the treatment

What is CranioSacral Therapy?

Few structures in the human body have as much influence over its ability to function properly as the brain and spinal cord that comprise the central nervous system. And few systems have as much impact on the brain and spinal cord as the membranes and fluid that surround and protect them — the craniosacral system. Every day the body endures stresses and strains and the structures compensate. Unfortunately, these compensations can cause fascia to tighten and distort the craniosacral system, which in turn can put pressure on the brain and spinal cord. The result? A barrier to the healthy performance of the central nervous system — and potentially every other system with which it interacts.
More than 40 years ago, osteopathic physician John E. Upledger developed a set of gentle techniques to release those restrictions and imbalances. After years of university research and testing, he named his new method CranioSacral Therapy (CST).
Practitioners use a soft touch — roughly the weight of a nickel — to evaluate the craniosacral system. Specific techniques are then used to release any restrictions or imbalances they find, creating the best possible environment for the brain and spinal cord. This naturally helps eliminate the negative effects of stress, strengthens resistance to disease, and enhances overall health and well-being.
Why Study CranioSacral Therapy?

Studying CranioSacral Therapy is not only an intrinsically rewarding path to pursue by itself, it’s also beneficial to add to your toolkit if you’re a physician, nurse, chiropractor, psychologist, initiative healer, masseuse, yoga teacher, healthcare or wellness professional.

CranioSacral Therapy is used to treat a range of ailments, from the physical to the neurological to the psychological. It has proven particularly effective in address a wide range of health complaints:

items: Most common: stress, headaches, neck and back pain, TMJ
More elusive: neurovascular and immune disorders, fibromyalgia and other connective-tissue disorders, ADD/ADHD, emotional difficulties
Most challenging: brain injury and disorders,autism, motor coordination, physical birth defects.

blocks.text: The areas of focus will be on the skeletal & fascial system. You’ll also study theoretical concepts of craniosacral therapy, and practice highly specialized observational skills that help attune you to the client’s physical state and any underlying symptoms or issues.

Not only will you delicately manipulate the bones of the head and the base of the spine in order to restore an optimal, balanced flow of cerebrospinal fluid and other subtle energies within the body, you’ll learn to help others to optimal health on a much deeper level beyond the physical body.

Therapeutic Synergy
CST is an ideal complement to massage therapy. The techniques help practitioners refine their palpation skills and address soft tissues both intradurally and extradurally. It’s also so gentle on the hands that many massage therapists practice CST as their primary modality.

Neurological Benefits
Because CST works to improve central nervous system function, it can be a beneficial adjunctive therapy for those clients with neurological involvement, particularly children. One of CST’s principal benefits is its ability to reverse the effects of stress by providing conditions in which the central nervous system can rest and rejuvenate. Examples of such stress-related problems include insomnia, chronic fatigue, migraine headaches, poor digestion, anxiety and TMJ syndrome...

Chronic Solutions
CST also helps patients suffering from chronic symptoms that have not been relieved by allopathic approaches. These conditions include traumatic brain and spinal cord injuries, whiplash sequelae, motor-coordination impairments, chronic neck and back pain, scoliosis, emotional difficulties, learning disabilities, post-traumatic stress disorder, orthopedic problems and many other conditions.

What is CranioSacral Therapy?

Few structures in the human body have as much influence over its ability to function properly as the brain and spinal cord that comprise the central nervous system. And few systems have as much impact on the brain and spinal cord as the membranes and fluid that surround and protect them — the craniosacral system. Every day the body endures stresses and strains and the structures compensate. Unfortunately, these compensations can cause fascia to tighten and distort the craniosacral system, which in turn can put pressure on the brain and spinal cord. The result? A barrier to the healthy performance of the central nervous system — and potentially every other system with which it interacts.
More than 40 years ago, osteopathic physician John E. Upledger developed a set of gentle techniques to release those restrictions and imbalances. After years of university research and testing, he named his new method CranioSacral Therapy (CST).
Practitioners use a soft touch — roughly the weight of a nickel — to evaluate the craniosacral system. Specific techniques are then used to release any restrictions or imbalances they find, creating the best possible environment for the brain and spinal cord. This naturally helps eliminate the negative effects of stress, strengthens resistance to disease, and enhances overall health and well-being.
Why Study CranioSacral Therapy?

Studying CranioSacral Therapy is not only an intrinsically rewarding path to pursue by itself, it’s also beneficial to add to your toolkit if you’re a physician, nurse, chiropractor, psychologist, initiative healer, masseuse, yoga teacher, healthcare or wellness professional.

CranioSacral Therapy is used to treat a range of ailments, from the physical to the neurological to the psychological. It has proven particularly effective in address a wide range of health complaints:

items: Most common: stress, headaches, neck and back pain, TMJ
More elusive: neurovascular and immune disorders, fibromyalgia and other connective-tissue disorders, ADD/ADHD, emotional difficulties
Most challenging: brain injury and disorders,autism, motor coordination, physical birth defects.

blocks.text: The areas of focus will be on the skeletal & fascial system. You’ll also study theoretical concepts of craniosacral therapy, and practice highly specialized observational skills that help attune you to the client’s physical state and any underlying symptoms or issues.

Not only will you delicately manipulate the bones of the head and the base of the spine in order to restore an optimal, balanced flow of cerebrospinal fluid and other subtle energies within the body, you’ll learn to help others to optimal health on a much deeper level beyond the physical body.

Therapeutic Synergy
CST is an ideal complement to massage therapy. The techniques help practitioners refine their palpation skills and address soft tissues both intradurally and extradurally. It’s also so gentle on the hands that many massage therapists practice CST as their primary modality.

Neurological Benefits
Because CST works to improve central nervous system function, it can be a beneficial adjunctive therapy for those clients with neurological involvement, particularly children. One of CST’s principal benefits is its ability to reverse the effects of stress by providing conditions in which the central nervous system can rest and rejuvenate. Examples of such stress-related problems include insomnia, chronic fatigue, migraine headaches, poor digestion, anxiety and TMJ syndrome...

Chronic Solutions
CST also helps patients suffering from chronic symptoms that have not been relieved by allopathic approaches. These conditions include traumatic brain and spinal cord injuries, whiplash sequelae, motor-coordination impairments, chronic neck and back pain, scoliosis, emotional difficulties, learning disabilities, post-traumatic stress disorder, orthopedic problems and many other conditions.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.q: What is your cancellation policy?

a.text: All bookings are final. No refunds, credits or transfers allowed.

items.q: What costs are not covered?

a.text: You are responsible for any travel expenses such as air ticket, outside hotel, etc. and personal expenses such as shopping, outside meals, etc.

items.q: What airport do I fly into Bali?

a.text: You will fly into Denpasar International Airport (DPS).

items.q: Do you offer airport transfers?

a.text: Yes, Lumeria can arrange airport pick-up and drop-off for an additional charge. Otherwise, you may use Ground Transportation or Grab app – both options are available at the airport, safe and convenient.

items.q: What currency of money do I need?

a.text: Bali, Indonesia uses Rupiah IDR. Your country’s currency may be exchanged at airport arrivals or any Currency Exchange stations.

items.q: Where can I get my laundry cleaned?

a.text: Lumeria provides laundry service at an additional charge.

items.q: What should I pack for this retreat?

a.text: Bali Ubud is a tropical climate and July is typically the most comfortable month with sunny weather. Pack yoga clothes, comfortable clothes, pajamas and any personal sundries and belongings you typically require for yourself during your travels.

items.q: Do I need to pack a yoga mat?

a.text: It is not necessary as we will provide yoga mats, yoga props, drinking water and all materials needed for this retreat. However, you’re more than welcome to bring your own yoga mat, if you prefer to use your own.

items.q: I am new to yoga. Is this retreat suitable for me?

a.text: Our classes and all sessions are beginner friendly and no prior experience is required. Everyone is welcome.

items.q: Do I need to do anything in advance to prepare for this retreat?

a.text: No, simply come with an open heart and willingness to receive, practice and heal.

items.q: Is there someone I can talk with if I have more specific questions?

a.text: We are here for you and happy to answer all your questions. Please email us at info@lumeriayoga.com and our team will contact you directly.
